findings.title: appendStep writes and publishes the step before it charges, so a failed charge leaves a receipt with no cost, against the promise in worker.ts
findings.scenario: A worker calls appendStep(task, 'tool', 'search: x', {tool:'search', cost:{dollars:0.01}}). trace.addCost rejects (with Postgres, billing's recordSpend runs inside that transaction and can throw). The step row is already committed and step.appended is already sent. The page shows 'search ... $0.01' for ever, the task's ownCost and the session spend stay 0, the ledger has no entry. worker.ts line 22-23 says the receipt and the cost 'cannot disagree'.
findings.evidence: Ran a probe in an exported copy of the branch (git archive to /tmp, not the working tree): Kernel over a MemoryTrace whose addCost throws. Snapshot after idle(): steps:[{kind:'tool', detail:{tool:'search', cost:{dollars:0.01}}}], task.status:'failed', ownCost:{dollars:0}, spend:{dollars:0}. Code: `await this.writeStep(taskId, kind, text, kept); ... await this.addSpend(taskId, kept.cost, ...)` are two separate writes; PgTrace.appendStep and PgTrace.addCost each open their own withTransaction.

findings.title: The rule 'detail.cost is charged, do not also call addSpend' is only in worker.ts; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md still teaches report.addSpend(task, $0.01, "search"), and nothing stops the double charge
findings.scenario: The steering author follows the sequence diagrams in ARCHITECTURE.md (line 561 and line 718: `W->>K: report.addSpend(childId, $0.01)`) and also fills detail.cost so that the page shows the price, as the spec page does. Each search is charged twice to the task and to the billing ledger. No error, no log: the user pays double.
findings.evidence: Ran a probe: worker does appendStep(id,'tool','search: x',{cost:{dollars:0.01}}) then addSpend(id,{dollars:0.01},'search'). Result: ownCost {dollars:0.02}, status 'ended'. The warning exists at apps/server/src/core/domain/worker.ts:22-24, which is the right first place, but addSpend's own docstring only says 'for a spend that is not a step's', and the branch does not touch docs/ARCHITECTURE.md at all (git diff --stat shows no docs file). The class diagram at ARCHITECTURE.md:385 also still shows `appendStep(taskId, step) Promise~Step~`.

findings.title: delegate() now always writes its own delegate step, so a worker that writes one first (the pattern on main, and the one ARCHITECTURE.md draws) gets two delegate blocks, and cannot say in words why it delegated
findings.scenario: A worker written against main does appendStep(id,'delegate','delegated 2 in parallel') and then delegate(id, [...]). It still compiles. The trace holds two delegate steps with the same text. On the page childrenByStep gives every child to the kernel's step (it names them), so the worker's step draws a DELEGATED block with no children under it. The kernel's text is fixed (`delegated ${n} in parallel`), so a worker has no way to put its own sentence on the delegate step.
findings.evidence: Ran a probe with that worker. Delegate steps in the snapshot: [{index:0, kind:'delegate', text:'delegated 2 in parallel'}, {index:1, kind:'delegate', text:'delegated 2 in parallel', detail:{childTaskIds:[...2 ids]}}]. This is a behaviour change of WorkerReport.delegate, not an addition. It is documented in worker.ts:24-25 and 29, but 'delegate' stays an accepted kind for appendStep, so nothing refuses the old pattern. origin/steering/sandbox-foundations does not implement Worker yet (its core/domain/worker.ts is the Sprint 1 two-argument appendStep, its steering/index.ts says 'worker/compute ... are not here yet'), so nobody is broken today; the trap is for the next author.

findings.title: StepDetail.output and rows have no bound and no preview: the whole text is stored, sent in step.appended and sent again in every snapshot
findings.scenario: A real 'run' tool passes a process's stdout as detail.output. A 5 MB log is written to the jsonb column, published to every socket of the session in one frame, and returned by every GET /api/sessions/:id and every session.open after that. ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 designed `preview: string | null // first lines; full text via step.full` for this reason; StepDetail dropped the split and added no limit in its place.
findings.evidence: Ran a probe: appendStep(id,'tool','run: big',{output:'x'.repeat(5_000_000)}) is accepted; the snapshot step has detail.output.length 5000000. Kernel.appendStep checks only childTaskIds and cost. The contract comment for output says only 'Shown in a fixed-width block'.

findings.title: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 still shows a different Step, and the contract comment that tied the two together was deleted
findings.scenario: A reader of section 4 sees Step with top-level id, tool, title, state, startedAt, endedAt, cost, preview, childTaskIds. The contract now has tool, cost and childTaskIds nested under an optional `detail`, durationMs in place of startedAt/endedAt, and rows/output that section 4 does not have. The old comment in sessions.ts ('The richer step ... in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 lands with the steering slice and adds fields, never repurposes these') was replaced with 'One line of a task's trace, and what it carried', so neither file says which one is the truth. The change itself is additive; the design doc is now wrong about it.
findings.evidence: git show session/rich-steps:docs/ARCHITECTURE.md lines 155-171 against packages/contracts/src/sessions.ts lines 26-62. The branch diff touches no file under docs/. What StepDetail left out that the spec page 04 needs: (1) `state` and a start time, so a step cannot be shown while it runs. The spec draws 'run 2 m 41 s' live and thinking text streaming (`data-stream`); on this contract a step appears only after it ends, since appendStep is write-once with durationMs. (2) a step `id`, which section 4's streamText(stepId, delta) and step.full need. (3) the 'tool call' meta and the save/record blocks fit `rows` and need nothing more.

findings.title: The session README still describes the old demo worker and its 'Public index' block omits the new exports
findings.scenario: The README says demoWorker is 'a lead that fans out to three readers, each of which spends and replies' and lists the exports as buildTree, TaskNode, Node, Kernel. On the branch demoWorker is a factory with paceMs, readers search, run, record a finding and reply, index.ts also exports `demoWorker` and `DemoOptions`, and main.ts imports it from there. The README says nothing on step detail, on the charge inside appendStep, or on the delegate step now being the kernel's.
findings.evidence: git grep on the branch finds one mention of demoWorker in the README (line 23) and no mention of detail, appendStep or addSpend. index.ts diff: `export { demoWorker, type DemoOptions } from './demoWorker.js';`.

checked_and_fine: packages/contracts: every change is additive. Step.detail and step.appended.detail are optional, StepRow and StepDetail are new types, no existing field changed type or meaning, STEP_KINDS is unchanged.
npm run typecheck (tsc --build plus the web tsconfig) is green on an exported copy of the branch, so every current consumer compiles.

apps/server/src/modules/projects, billing, identity and core: git grep finds no use of Step, StepDetail, step.appended, appendStep or demoWorker outside the session slice and core/domain/worker.ts. Nothing there depends on the changed shapes.
A worker written against main that uses appendStep(id, kind, text) and addSpend separately still compiles and charges once (probe B: reader tasks charged 0.01 each through addSpend only).

demoWorker changed from a value to a factory, but main's session/index.ts did not export it, so no other slice could hold the old value; the only callers (index.ts default, main.ts, tests) are updated.
main.ts imports demoWorker through the public index './modules/session/index.js', not a file inside the slice.

origin/steering/sandbox-foundations: it does not implement Worker or call WorkerReport yet. Its core/domain/worker.ts and contracts are the older Sprint 1 versions, so it must rebase in any case. It will conflict textually with this branch in main.ts and .env.example (both add lines in the same places); no semantic conflict found.
appendStep refuses a worker-supplied childTaskIds, including an empty array (probe D: the task failed and no step was written), and checks the cost with recordable() before anything is written.
A zero cost, or one that rounds to zero, writes the receipt and makes no charge (`kept.cost.dollars > 0`).

Migration 008 is additive (nullable jsonb column, with a Down); PgTrace maps a null column to an absent `detail`, not `detail: null`; the detail is stringified before insert so that `rows` does not go as a Postgres array. traceContract.ts has a round-trip test for both implementations. I did not run the Postgres half: no database was started.
The web reducer keeps the whole event minus `type`, so later additive fields on step.appended reach the page without another change. It does not add money.
childrenByStep falls back to counting for delegate steps recorded before the field existed, so old rows in the database still draw their children.
